clauses.reason: Provision 1-101 amends Section 1-101 of Executive Order No. 12201, effective July 28, 1980, to authorize the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System to set uniform requirements for changes in terms in open-end consumer credit accounts, with that authorization revoked as of October 31, 1980. The amendment is self-executing: it was performed when its stated effective date, July 28, 1980, arrived, so the command is exhausted by performance on 1980-07-28 (the signing date, July 3, 1980, is earlier but the order defers the amendment). The amended text of Executive Order No. 12201 and its October 31, 1980 revocation are consequences of the performed amendment, not continuing commands of this order.

Provision 1-102 revokes the authorization granted by Section 1-102 of Executive Order No. 12201 (credit extended by certain financial intermediaries) as of August 11, 1980. A revocation is performed when its stated date arrives, so the command is exhausted by performance on 1980-08-11; the revocation of the authorization survives as a consequence.

Provision 1-103 revokes the authorizations granted by Sections 1-103 and 1-104 of Executive Order No. 12201 (credit extended to nonmember commercial banks in the form of managed liabilities, and record keeping) as of July 28, 1980. A revocation is performed when its stated date arrives, so the command is exhausted by performance on 1980-07-28; the revocation survives as a consequence.

Provision 1-104 amends Section 1-105 of Executive Order No. 12201, effective July 28, 1980, so that it defines only consumer credit and open-end credit by reference to the regulations of the Board of Governors. The amendment is self-executing and was performed when July 28, 1980 arrived, so the command is exhausted by performance on 1980-07-28; the amended definition survives as part of Executive Order No. 12201 and is treated in that order's claim.

Provision 1-105 revokes Section 1-106 of Executive Order No. 12201, the provision saying the authorizations remain in effect for an indefinite period until revoked by the President. It states no later effective date, and the order is signed July 3, 1980, so the revocation is treated as performed on signing, 1980-07-03; the alternative reading from Federal Register publication, July 7, 1980, is not a stated effective date. The command is exhausted by performance and the revocation survives as a consequence.

research_rationale:
Identity confirmed against the census register (executive order of 1980-07-03, Credit Control Revocation) and the held Federal Register text at 45 FR 45571, whose text layer shows Vol. 45, No. 131, Monday, July 7, 1980. The order has five numbered provisions, each a self-executing amendment or revocation of Executive Order No. 12201 with its own stated effective date (July 28, August 11 or, for the last, no date). Each is exhausted by performance on that date; the latest is August 11, 1980. No later held text cites this order other than Executive Order No. 12201 itself, so no later instrument reaches it.

savings.reason: The amended and revoked provisions of Executive Order No. 12201, and the October 31, 1980 revocation written into amended Section 1-101 of that order, are lasting consequences of the performed commands; actions taken by the Board of Governors under Executive Order No. 12201 before each stated date are accrued. This order continues no authorization.
